entries.title: How can a banana grow without big seeds?
entries.answer: A wild banana can have hard, noticeable seeds, but the Cavendish bananas sold in many stores usually have no mature seeds. The fruit can grow without the usual process of making seeds. Growers keep those plants going by starting new plants from living pieces that grow near an older plant or by other methods that copy its growth. The new plants make very similar fruit. Tiny dark specks in a store banana are much smaller than the hard seeds in many wild bananas.
facts: Wild bananas often have seeds much bigger than the tiny specks in a Cavendish banana.

questions.text: Why can a banana count as a fruit without mature seeds inside?
What other plant can start more plants without growing new seeds?
How can growing a seed change the traits you get?

entries.title: How can a bean be a pod or a seed on your plate?
entries.answer: A bean plant grows long pods around its seeds. In green beans, people often eat the soft pods along with young seeds. Other varieties can stay on the plant until the seeds are mature and the pods dry. The seeds that came out of those pods may then be sold as dried beans. Bean plants can grow in different shapes. A bush bean stays lower and more compact, while a pole bean can stretch up a support to reach more light.
facts: Some bean plants grow as bushes, while others climb.

questions.text: Why are some pea pods eaten whole too?
What helps a climbing bean plant reach upward?
Where does a different kind of bean relative grow its pods?

entries.title: How can a greenhouse grow plants when it is cold outside?
entries.answer: Clear parts of a greenhouse let sunlight reach the plants and surfaces inside. The light can warm those surfaces. The walls and roof slow the mixing between the warmer inside air and colder air outdoors. Plants can get a warmer place to grow even if there is snow nearby. A greenhouse can still get too cold at night or too warm in bright sun. Growers can store some daytime warmth, add heat, or open vents when the plants need cooler air.
facts: A greenhouse often has openings that let extra heat escape on warm days.

questions.text: Why do the plants still need sunlight inside the greenhouse?
What happens to water released from the leaves inside?
Can plants get the materials they need without garden soil?

entries.title: How can cabbage and cauliflower be close relatives?
entries.answer: Cabbage and cauliflower look different because growers choose plants for different parts. Many cabbages make a ball of closely packed leaves. Cauliflower growers often want a tight head made from developing flower shoots. Both vegetables are forms of the same plant species, as are broccoli and kale. Over many generations, people saved seeds from plants that grew in useful ways. Similar plant relatives can end up with different shapes when their leaves or shoots grow to different sizes.
facts: Kale, broccoli, cabbage and cauliflower are cultivated forms of Brassica oleracea.

questions.text: What makes the bumps you see when you look closely at a broccoli head?
Why can seed choices change what grows in a garden later?
What important jobs do large cabbage leaves still have?

entries.title: How can cream turn into butter?
entries.answer: Cream contains many small drops of milk fat in a watery liquid. Churning moves the cream around until more of the drops bump together and stick. Eventually, the fat collects in soft pieces. Some watery liquid can drain away. That leaves a material with a much bigger share of milk fat, which is butter. Churning changes the way the parts of cream are arranged. It is different from turning water into ice, because the fat and watery part of the cream end up separated.
facts: The watery part that can drain away during traditional churning is called buttermilk.

questions.text: How can very small drops of one liquid stay mixed in another?
What different milk ingredients are gathered together in cheese?
What else changes the feel of a food made with cream?

entries.title: How can egg white turn into a fluffy foam?
entries.answer: Whipping egg white draws air into the liquid and breaks it into many small bubbles. Some of the proteins in the egg white unfold and collect near the bubbles, helping build a thin film that keeps them from popping so fast. The air takes up space, so the egg white can become a tall foam. A baker can use that foam to make a food feel lighter. The bubbles are small, but there can be a great many in one spoonful.
facts: A foam contains a lot of little bubbles mixed into another material.

questions.text: How does heating change egg white proteins?
How does a thin film of liquid hold a pocket of air?
Why do ice cream makers stir the mixture as it freezes?

entries.title: How can plants grow without soil?
entries.answer: A plant needs water, minerals, light and suitable air, but it may not have to get those supplies from soil. In hydroponics, a grower can send water with dissolved nutrients to the roots. A frame or small container can hold the plant up while roots reach the wet part. Roots also need oxygen, so the system can let some roots meet air or carry oxygen into the water. The plants must still catch enough light to make their own sugars.
facts: Some hydroponic crops rest in a holder while roots reach a water supply.

questions.text: What do roots do even when there is no soil around them?
How can a greenhouse make warm growing conditions?
What useful jobs does soil normally help carry out in a garden?

entries.title: How can you build a garden in shallow water?
entries.answer: In the lakes near the old Aztec capital, farmers made raised beds called chinampas. Mud and plant material helped build up long plots with canals between them. Trees along the edge could help keep the beds in place. Farmers reached the plots by boat, and water nearby helped them grow crops. Chinampas look like islands from the canals, but the beds are built up from the bottom rather than floating. People still care for some of these gardens in Mexico City.
facts: Xochimilco has working chinampas as well as canals.

questions.text: What city used canals, roads, and gardens together?
Why was maize an important crop in early American farming?
What other ways can farmers get water to crops?

entries.title: How do farmers water crops when it does not rain?
entries.answer: Irrigation means bringing water to a place where plants need it. A farm may get water from a river, a well, or a place where water has been stored. Sprinklers send water through the air. Other systems let water move along channels, or drip it near each plant’s roots. How much water a farmer uses depends on the soil, crop, weather, and other conditions. Irrigation can help crops grow when the ground is dry, but the water still has to come from a supply that can meet the farm’s needs.
facts: Drip irrigation releases water slowly near plants.
Irrigation water can come from below ground or from an above-ground source.

questions.text: How did people in ancient Egypt use river water to grow food?
How did Roman aqueducts use gravity to move water?
Why might a farmer change which crop grows in a field?

entries.title: How do scraps turn into compost?
entries.answer: A compost pile gives little animals and other living things a place to break down dead leaves, plant scraps and similar materials. They use some parts as food. Given enough air and moisture, they gradually make a dark, crumbly mixture called compost. The finished material can be mixed into soil, where it can help roots by improving the soil around them. It takes time for living things to change fresh leaves and scraps into compost with no obvious pieces left.
facts: Compost can help soil keep more water available to plants.

questions.text: Why can some fungi take apart fallen branches?
What is organic matter doing in a garden bed?
How can a covering help the top of soil keep moisture?

entries.title: How do wheat kernels turn into flour?
entries.answer: Wheat plants make dry kernels. A mill breaks the kernels into pieces and can sift the pieces by how big they are. The soft, food-storing middle can become fine white flour. Whole wheat flour includes the outer bran and the small part that could start a new plant as well. Different sorts of wheat have qualities that make their flour useful for different foods. A baker may choose a flour that holds up well for bread and pick a different one for a delicate cake.
facts: Some mills separate parts of a wheat kernel so they can be used in different products.

questions.text: Can a flour still count as a whole grain?
What makes gas bubbles in the dough when flour becomes bread?
How can another grain change when it is milled?

entries.title: How does a cacao seed become chocolate?
entries.answer: Making chocolate begins with cacao seeds surrounded by pulp. Changes during fermentation help develop the flavors. The seeds are later dried and usually roasted. After the shell is removed, little pieces called nibs can be ground into a paste. The paste contains both cocoa solids and fat called cocoa butter. A chocolate maker can mix in other ingredients and work the mixture until it has the smoothness and flavor they want. The original seed no longer looks like a seed in a bar.
facts: Crushed pieces of roasted cacao seed are called nibs.

questions.text: Where are the chocolate-making seeds found before harvest?
How can heating change the smells and colors of food?
Which other fruit supplies seeds that people roast?

entries.title: How does cotton grow on a plant?
entries.answer: A cotton plant makes a dry fruit often called a boll. Inside that fruit, fine soft hairs grow from the surface of the seeds. When the fruit opens, the hairs spread out and give it a fluffy white look. To make fabric, people separate the fibers from the seeds. Next, the fibers can be gathered and twisted into a yarn. A piece of cotton cloth began with hairs a plant grew around its seeds rather than with strips cut from its leaves.
facts: The puffy fibers grow around and on cotton seeds.

questions.text: Why can a dry pod count as a fruit from a flowering plant?
What other plants use soft or fluffy parts around their seeds?
How do fibers that grow on a plant become cloth?

entries.title: How does liquid milk become solid cheese?
entries.answer: In many kinds of cheese making, a change in milk makes its proteins gather to form soft parts called curds. A watery liquid called whey can drain away. The cheese maker can then shape the curds. Choices about what stays inside, how much it is pressed, and whether the cheese is aged help produce cheeses with different textures. A fresh cheese can hold a fair amount of water and feel soft. A cheese that loses more water can become much firmer.
facts: Cheese makers can leave different amounts of water in the curds.

questions.text: How can milk thicken into yogurt while keeping much of its liquid?
What part of cream comes together when butter is made?
How can part of milk be separated from the rest of the mixture?

entries.title: How does tree sap become maple syrup?
entries.answer: In places with suitable weather, maple sap can flow well when nights are cold and days warm in late winter or spring. Sap from a sugar maple is usually clear and contains much more water than sugar. Makers collect it and remove a lot of the water so a smaller amount of sweeter liquid remains. Heating allows water to leave as vapor. Maple syrup is thicker than the sap that came out of the tree because the remaining liquid holds more sugar in each spoonful.
facts: Sugar maples are commonly tapped for sap.

questions.text: What tissue carries water and dissolved materials through a tree?
Why can clear sap contain some dissolved sugar?
What happens to sugar as a solution becomes more concentrated?

entries.title: How does yeast make bread rise?
entries.answer: Bread yeast is a tiny living fungus. When it finds sugars available in dough, it can use them and release carbon dioxide gas. The gas gathers in pockets held by the dough. Over time those pockets grow, lifting the dough so it takes up more space. That is what bakers mean when they say bread is rising. The bread keeps many of the pockets after it bakes, which makes it easier to bite than a solid baked lump of flour and water.
facts: Bakers add yeast to many breads to produce carbon dioxide gas.

questions.text: What larger part can another kind of fungus grow?
How can some batters make gas without yeast?
Why can the outside of the bread change color as it heats?

entries.title: What are all the little bumps on broccoli?
entries.answer: The green head of broccoli holds a tight group of unopened flower buds. The small bumps you see are those buds gathered on branching stems. People usually pick the head before the buds open. If they are left to grow, the buds can turn into many small yellow flowers, so the head no longer looks the same. The stalk is also a plant stem. A bite of broccoli can include both stems and the parts that would have become open flowers.
facts: An unpicked broccoli cluster can open into many little yellow flowers.

questions.text: What might appear when a bud opens all the way?
What are some other foods grown from close relatives of broccoli?
Which vegetable is a shoot rather than a group of flower buds?

entries.title: What are the little spears on an asparagus plant?
entries.answer: An asparagus spear is a young shoot that rises from a long-living part of the plant underground. People pick these shoots while they are still tender. If a shoot is left to grow, it elongates and grows many fine branches. The tall growth can look a little like a fern. It uses sunlight during the growing season and helps supply food for the parts below ground. Later that stored food helps a new crop of shoots start again.
facts: The underground asparagus crown can grow new shoots in more than one year.

questions.text: What jobs can a stem carry out as more leaves grow from it?
Which common vegetable is a thick root instead of a young stem?
What other plant uses food stored below ground to send up a shoot?

entries.title: What does pasteurized mean on a milk carton?
entries.answer: Pasteurizing milk means a dairy heats it for a carefully measured time and then cools it. The process reduces harmful germs so the milk is safer to drink. It does not make regular milk keep forever. People usually still store it cold and use it while fresh. Some drinks made from fruit are pasteurized as well. The process uses heat to make a food safer while keeping much of what people expect from the original food, such as the taste and texture.
facts: After heating for pasteurization, milk is cooled as part of processing.

questions.text: What do yogurt makers want certain useful bacteria to do later?
How is removing water a different way to help foods keep longer?
How does freezing change the texture of a fruit?

entries.title: What fruit does chocolate start from?
entries.answer: Chocolate begins on a cacao tree, which grows in warm, wet places. Its fruits are thick pods with ridged sides. They can grow on the trunk and branches instead of hanging only from the far ends of twigs. When a ripe pod is opened, it holds seeds surrounded by soft pulp. People call those seeds cacao beans even though cacao is from a different family than garden beans. The seeds can go through several changes before chocolate tastes the way we recognize.
facts: Cacao fruits can grow right from the trunk or a thick branch.

questions.text: What happens to a cacao seed before it becomes chocolate?
What about a cacao pod makes it a fruit?
What other drink starts from a seed held inside a fruit?

entries.title: What happens to old leaves in the soil?
entries.answer: A leaf that falls into soil can become food for little animals, fungi and other living things. They break it into smaller parts. Some of those materials stay in the soil in changed forms. Together with pieces of roots and other once-living things, they are part of the soil’s organic matter. This material can help soil hold water and make nutrients available to plants. A fresh leaf and a bit of dark older soil can belong to the same long recycling process.
facts: Some organic matter stays mixed into soil much longer than a fresh leaf lasts.

questions.text: How can fungi break down a fallen branch?
What do roots collect from what surrounds them?
How do soil’s mineral particles differ from remains of leaves?

entries.title: What is a pea pod holding?
entries.answer: A pea pod begins as part of a flower. It grows around several seeds, which are the round peas you may see lined up inside. Some varieties have tough pods and are grown mainly for the peas. A snow pea has a thin pod that people often eat while the seeds are still small. A sugar snap pea has a thicker edible pod. Pea plants usually grow well in cooler weather, which is why many gardeners start them before summer’s hottest days.
facts: Pea plants can hold on to supports with curling tendrils.

questions.text: Which part of a blossom can grow into a pod?
How are pea pods and bean pods alike?
What kind of frame gives a climbing pea something to grip?

entries.title: What makes a kernel of popcorn burst open?
entries.answer: A popcorn kernel has a little water inside, a lot of starch, and a tough outer coat. Heat makes some of its water turn into steam. The steam pushes on the coat until it breaks. The soft starch can then expand very fast. As it cools, the expanded starch stays in the fluffy shape you see in a bowl. A kernel with a damaged coat can leak steam too soon, which helps explain why some kernels stay unpopped.
facts: A popcorn kernel has a tough outer coat that can hold steam until it bursts.

questions.text: Where did people first develop corn as a crop?
How does a change in pressure affect a different kind of gas?
How can gas make another grain food puff up?

entries.title: What makes fruit jam thick enough to spread?
entries.answer: A lot of fruits contain a substance called pectin. Under the right conditions, pectin molecules form a loose network that can hold water. That network gives some fruit spreads a soft, thick texture. Sugar and acid can help certain kinds of pectin form a useful network. Jam often keeps mashed or chopped fruit, while jelly often starts with clear juice. Each can feel thick on a spoon even though much of it is still water.
facts: Jam often keeps some fruit pieces, while jelly usually begins with strained juice.

questions.text: How does removing much more water change a fruit’s feel?
Why can adding a lot of dissolved sugar change a liquid mixture?
What different food thickens when parts of a liquid gather together?

entries.title: What makes ice cream feel smooth instead of icy?
entries.answer: As ice cream freezes, some of its water forms solid ice crystals. A mixture with many tiny crystals can feel smooth on your tongue. Large crystals are easier to notice as gritty bits. Machines stir the cold mixture as it freezes to help keep crystals small and add air. In a freezer, a carton can warm a little when the door stays open. If some ice melts and freezes again, crystals may grow larger and make the texture feel different.
facts: An ice cream machine can stir a mixture while it freezes.

questions.text: What is the pattern inside an ordinary ice crystal?
What can happen to dissolved material when the temperature changes?
What other food has tiny drops of one liquid mixed through another?

entries.title: Where did corn come from?
entries.answer: Corn, also called maize, grew into a farm crop from a wild plant called teosinte. This change began thousands of years ago in what is now Mexico. People saved seeds from plants they wanted to grow again. Over many generations, the plants changed a great deal, including the size and shape of the part that holds the kernels. Farmers in different regions grew many kinds of maize. Today, an ear of maize can look very different depending on which variety it is.

sections.heading: Tiny clues
sections.text: Researchers in Mexico found tiny traces of maize on ancient tools. Even when a whole cob has disappeared, those traces can help scientists find when people were using the crop.

facts: Maize was grown in the Americas long before it reached Europe.
Evidence from one site in Mexico suggests maize was present there by about 8,700 years ago.

questions.text: Where is the present-day country in which maize first became a crop?
Why might a farmer grow different kinds of plants in the same field over time?
Where are varieties kept so future farmers can still grow them?

entries.title: Where does vanilla flavor come from?
entries.answer: Vanilla can come from the fruit of a climbing orchid. People often call the long fruit a vanilla bean, even though it is an orchid pod. Its flower must receive pollen to make that pod, and growers in many places pollinate the flowers by hand. The green pods do not start with the same strong scent as finished vanilla. A process of drying and other changes develops the familiar smell used to flavor foods. Small dark seeds can be seen inside some cured pods.
facts: Vanilla pods grow from the flowers of a climbing orchid.

questions.text: Which flower part can grow into a long fruit?
Which other flavor starts with material grown inside a tropical fruit?
What has to reach a flower before many plants can begin producing seeds?

entries.title: Where on a pumpkin vine does a pumpkin begin?
entries.answer: A pumpkin vine sends its stems across the ground. It can make flowers that release pollen and other flowers where fruits can start. Below some flowers there is already a small shape that looks like a tiny pumpkin. If pollen reaches that flower and the plant can support a fruit, the shape can swell into a pumpkin. Seeds grow inside as it gets bigger. A bee may visit both kinds of flowers while it is searching for food.
facts: A tiny round shape just below some pumpkin flowers is where a fruit can grow.

questions.text: Which part of a flower can hold future seeds?
Why does a pumpkin count as a fruit in plant science?
What might a gardener learn from starting a new plant with saved seeds?

entries.title: Which part of a carrot plant do we eat?
entries.answer: The familiar part of a carrot is a thick main root. It can hold food the plant made earlier in its green leaves. Inside the soil, smaller roots can branch out from the main one as the plant takes in water. The part sold in a store grows below the ground, but you can spot the plant in a garden by its leafy top. If the plant keeps growing instead of being harvested, the stored food can help it make new growth later.
facts: A carrot has a main taproot while its leafy tops grow above ground.

questions.text: What can roots gather as they grow farther into the soil?
Why does a potato count as a stem even though it grows underground?
What part of another plant do people harvest while it is still young?

entries.title: Why are coffee beans taken from cherries?
entries.answer: A coffee plant grows small fruits around seeds. People call the ripe fruits coffee cherries because many look rounded and red, like cherries. The “beans” used for coffee are the seeds taken from the fruit. A fruit often holds two of them. The seeds go through steps such as drying and roasting before people grind them. A coffee plant and a cherry tree are different plants, even though people use a name from one to describe the look of the other’s fruit.
facts: Arabica coffee often has two seeds inside one fruit.

questions.text: What other tropical tree hides useful seeds inside a fruit?
What changes can roasting bring out in cacao too?
Why can one part be a fruit while its contents are seeds?

entries.title: Why are raisins smaller than grapes?
entries.answer: A grape carries a lot of water inside it. When it is dried into a raisin, much of that water leaves and the skin wrinkles around the smaller fruit. Some of the sugar is still there, but there is less water with it. This can make raisins taste quite sweet in each small bite. Other fruits can also be dried. Drying changes their feel and weight, and it can help them keep longer by taking away water that many little living things need.
facts: A dried fruit can have a stronger sweet taste in the same-sized bite because it has less water.

questions.text: How can removing water from tree sap make it taste sweeter?
What changes if a food’s water freezes rather than leaves it?
What makes a fruit spread thick without drying it all the way?

entries.title: Why are there rows of trees along some fields?
entries.answer: A strong wind can carry loose soil off an open field. Rows of trees or shrubs can slow some of the air moving near the ground on the sheltered side. Farm planners call the planted rows a windbreak. They choose where to put the plants and how tall or dense to let them grow. This can reduce wind erosion and protect young crops. The rows may also leave places for birds and other living things to find shelter between the fields.
facts: A planted line of trees or shrubs used to slow wind can be called a windbreak.

questions.text: What living cover can protect the soil between seasons?
How can farmers manage water rolling down a slope?
Why can the size of soil particles matter when wind moves them?

entries.title: Why do apple growers join pieces of two trees?
entries.answer: A seed from a favorite apple can grow a tree, but the young tree may make apples with different qualities. Growers often attach a piece from a known apple tree to the roots and lower stem of another one. When the two parts grow together, the upper part can make the kind of apple the grower wants. The lower part may help control the tree’s size or handle certain soil conditions. This joining is called grafting.
facts: A graft can join a fruit-making top to roots suited for a particular garden.

questions.text: Why does a fruit orchard often grow more than one type of apple?
What do the connected stem tissues have to move across the graft?
Why may a seed grow into a plant different from its parent?

entries.title: Why do blueberry bushes like acidic soil?
entries.answer: Different plants grow best in different kinds of soil. Many blueberries do well in soil that is more acidic than the soil preferred by a lot of other garden crops. The soil’s acidity affects how easily the bush’s fine roots can get some nutrients. A grower may check the soil first instead of assuming that every garden bed will suit blueberries. Good pollination can help fruit grow, but healthy roots still need the right conditions for the whole bush to thrive.
facts: Blueberry bushes may have trouble taking up certain nutrients when their soil pH is too high.

questions.text: What does a lower pH tell a gardener about a watery sample?
How do roots get what a growing bush needs?
Why can another kind of fruit plant near a garden crop sometimes help it make fruit?

entries.title: Why do brown rice and white rice look different?
entries.answer: A rice grain grows inside a hard covering called a hull. A machine takes that outside covering off before the rice is eaten. Brown rice still has layers of bran and other parts around its lighter center. White rice is milled further to remove most of those remaining outer parts. This makes the grain look paler and can change how it feels after cooking. Rice can grow in different shapes and lengths, whether it is later sold as brown or white.
facts: Both brown rice and white rice are usually sold without their tough outside hulls.

questions.text: How do some farmers grow the crop before it goes to a mill?
What does a grain need to keep to be called whole?
What changes when oat grains go through a different kind of mill?

entries.title: Why do farmers change crops in a field?
entries.answer: Crop rotation means planning to grow different crops in the same place at different times. If a disease can easily spread among one kind of plant, growing an unrelated plant in that field for a while can leave the disease with fewer plants to infect. Different crops can also give the soil different kinds of roots and cover. The plan depends on the land. For example, a gardener growing beans after tomatoes is using a different rotation from a big farm alternating corn and soybeans.
facts: A crop rotation has a planned order that uses more than one kind of crop.
Rotation can help manage some plant diseases.

questions.text: Where did one major crop in modern rotations come from?
How do farmers supply water during a dry spell?
Where can researchers preserve seeds of several varieties?

entries.title: Why do gardeners cover soil with mulch?
entries.answer: A layer of straw, leaves or small wood chips can keep sun and wind from touching bare soil directly. This covering is called mulch. It shades the ground, which can slow water loss. It can also make it harder for some weed seedlings to find light. Different mulches behave in different ways, and plant-based materials often break down in time. A piece of mulch is on top of the soil at first, even when some of its smaller parts eventually mix in.
facts: A covering can block light from reaching many weed seedlings.

questions.text: What may happen when a plant-based mulch breaks down?
How can a living cover protect a field?
Why might bare sand feel and drain differently from bare clay?

entries.title: Why do oil-based dressings sometimes separate?
entries.answer: Oil and vinegar can look like a single cloudy liquid after you shake a dressing. The motion breaks the oil into drops and spreads them through the watery vinegar. A mixture like this is called an emulsion. The drops can eventually come together into a layer again. Some foods use an ingredient that sits where the oil and water meet. That can help the drops stay apart longer. Mayonnaise is an example in which ingredients in egg yolk help hold many tiny drops in place.
facts: Mayonnaise contains small drops of oil spread through a watery mixture.

questions.text: Why do plain water and oil soon form separate layers?
How can a different substance help water carry drops of grease?
What makes a dressing a mixture even if its tiny parts are hard to see?

entries.title: Why do orchards grow more than one kind of apple tree?
entries.answer: Many apple trees grow more fruit when their flowers receive pollen from a different, compatible kind of apple tree. An orchard can have several kinds flowering around the same time to provide that pollen. A bee that visits blossoms can pick pollen up at one tree and carry some to another. Later, fruit can form around seeds. An orchard worker also chooses where to grow trees and how far apart to plant them so leaves and flowers have room.
facts: Many apple trees produce more reliably with pollen from a compatible kind nearby.

questions.text: How can an insect help pollen reach another flower?
Why might the top and bottom of an orchard tree come from different plants?
Why do apple slices change color after an orchard apple is cut?

entries.title: Why do peanuts grow underground?
entries.answer: A peanut plant makes flowers above ground, but after flowering it grows a slender part that reaches downward. This part is called a peg. It carries the tiny beginning of a pod down into the soil. The pod can grow larger underground and form the peanuts inside. Peanuts belong to the pea and bean family. Most other plants in that family grow their pods where you can see them above the ground, so peanuts make an unusual garden crop.
facts: A peanut pod has seeds inside even though the plant grows the pod below ground.

questions.text: Where do many other legumes hold their pods?
How is a potato underground for a different reason?
Why does a shell with seeds inside count as a fruit in plant science?

entries.title: Why do people save seeds in seed banks?
entries.answer: A seed bank stores seeds so people can grow their plants again in the future. It may hold many varieties of one crop. Some varieties have useful differences, such as growing better in a dry place. For many crops, keeping seeds dry and cold helps them stay alive for a long time. Staff test seeds to see which ones still sprout. When a supply gets too low, the seed bank can arrange to grow plants and gather fresh seeds.

sections.heading: An extra copy
sections.text: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway keeps backup seed collections that belong to institutions around the world.

facts: Seeds can look almost the same while growing into different varieties.
The Svalbard vault is a backup for seed collections kept elsewhere.

questions.text: How did saving seeds over time help create corn as we know it?
Why do farmers choose different crops from one season to the next?
How does another kind of institution preserve things for later study?

entries.title: Why do rolled oats look flat?
entries.answer: An oat grain starts inside a tough covering that people remove before cooking it. The edible part left behind is a groat. One way to process groats is to cut them into small chunks. Those are steel-cut oats. Another way softens the groats with steam and presses them flat with rollers. Those are rolled oats. Flatter or smaller pieces can take in water faster as they cook, while larger pieces can stay chewy in a bowl for longer.
facts: A whole oat with its hard outside hull removed is called a groat.

questions.text: Can changing a grain’s shape leave all its main edible parts present?
How is making a fine flour different from flattening a grain?
What additional changes make a grain look whiter instead of just flatter?

entries.title: Why do some garden plants need a trellis?
entries.answer: A climbing plant may be good at reaching upward but have a stem too thin to stand high on its own. A frame called a trellis gives the stem or its little climbing parts places to grip. Peas can hang onto a string with curling parts called tendrils. Some beans wrap the stem itself around a support. The roots still feed water to the growing vine. Lifting leaves off the ground can also give the gardener an easier path between plants.
facts: A trellis supports climbing parts without taking over the work of the plant’s roots.

questions.text: How can a pea plant hold itself up?
What is the difference between a pole bean and a bush bean?
Why can lifting a stem help the plant’s leaves?

entries.title: Why do some rice fields look like ponds?
entries.answer: Some farmers place shallow water over a rice field during part of the growing season. Rice can grow in conditions that slow down some weeds, so standing water can help keep a field from getting crowded. Farmers use banks around sections of land to help hold the water. Rice fields do not always have to look flooded. Some growers use different water schedules or grow rice without a steady layer of water. Their choices depend on the place, the water supply and the type of rice.
facts: Some rice growers save water by changing when they flood their fields.

entries.title: Why do some rows curve around the side of a hill?
entries.answer: Water can run quickly down a field if rows lead straight downhill. Planting across the slope makes the rows follow the curves of the hill at about the same height. This is called contour farming. The rows can interrupt the flow so water moves more slowly and has more chances to soak into the ground. Slower runoff can carry away less soil. Curved rows are one tool a farmer can combine with other ways of keeping the ground covered.
facts: Contour planting follows paths at similar heights across a slope.

entries.title: Why do some soils feel gritty or sticky?
entries.answer: Soil contains mineral pieces of different sizes. Sand has the largest of the three common groups, so it often feels gritty. Silt is finer. Clay pieces are so small that wet clay-rich soil can feel sticky and smooth. Most soils have a mix of these sizes. The mix is called soil texture. It helps affect how fast water can move and how much stays between particles. The texture of a garden patch can differ from soil only a short walk away.
facts: Soil texture depends on the mix of sand, silt and clay particles.

entries.title: Why does clear egg white turn solid as it cooks?
entries.answer: An uncooked egg white is a watery mixture with many folded proteins in it. Heat makes some of those proteins unfold and catch on to one another. The connected proteins begin holding the water in a soft solid. The new arrangement also scatters light, which gives a cooked egg white its cloudy or white look. You can see both changes happen as the egg warms. It stops flowing freely as a liquid and begins to keep its own shape.
facts: Heat can change how parts of egg proteins are arranged.

entries.title: Why does garlic come apart into cloves?
entries.answer: The round piece of garlic in a kitchen is a bulb. Peel away its dry outer covering and you can see several smaller pieces called cloves. They are held together at the base while the plant grows. Each clove has stored food and can contain a bud for a new garlic plant. If one starts growing, its leaves can rise above ground while another bulb forms below. A garlic clove is one layer-built part of a whole bulb, rather than the seed inside a fruit.
facts: Each garlic clove can contain a bud that grows a new plant.

entries.title: Why does thawed fruit sometimes feel softer?
entries.answer: Inside a piece of fruit, little cells hold water and other materials. When fruit freezes, some of that water becomes ice crystals. Growing ice can damage parts of the cells and the tiny spaces between them. After thawing, juice can leak out more easily and the fruit can feel softer than before it froze. Fast freezing usually leads to smaller crystals, which can cause less damage. A soft thawed berry can still be useful in a food where firmness does not matter much.
facts: Faster freezing often gives ice crystals less time to grow before the fruit freezes through.

entries.title: Why does toast turn brown when it heats?
entries.answer: When a bread surface gets hot, some of its sugars react with pieces of proteins. These changes make new substances that can give toast its brown color and warm smell. Chemists call this family of changes the Maillard reaction. It happens on many heated foods, including the crust on a loaf. The inside of a slice often stays soft and pale because it holds more water and does not get as hot as the dry surface during a short time in the toaster.
facts: The Maillard reaction can also change the smell of food.

entries.title: Why is yogurt thicker than milk?
entries.answer: In yogurt making, certain helpful bacteria use some of the sugar in milk and produce lactic acid. The acid makes the milk more sour. It also changes how milk proteins fit together, so they can hold water in a soft network. That is why yogurt can stay on a spoon more easily than fresh milk. Some yogurt can release a thin layer of liquid on top if it sits. That layer comes from the mixture giving up a little water.
facts: Yogurt gets some of its tangy flavor from lactic acid.

entries.title: Why plant a crop that you may not harvest?
entries.answer: A cover crop is grown to do a job for the soil. Its leaves and roots can protect a field when a main crop is out of season. Roots help hold soil in place while the plants grow, and a cover may leave a layer of stems behind after it stops growing. A farmer can choose a crop based on the time available and what the field needs. The plants can matter even if nobody sends their grain or leaves to a store.
facts: Some cover crops are grown between seasons for the main crop.

entries.title: Will saved seeds grow into the same kind of plant?
entries.answer: A saved seed can start another plant, but the new plant may not be exactly like the old one. In many kinds of plants, pollen can come from a second plant, and the new seed can carry a mix of traits. If neighboring plants have different traits, a saved seed may grow up with a surprising combination. Gardens can still use carefully chosen seed to keep familiar varieties growing. Saving a seed and growing from a piece of a stem are different ways to start.
facts: A seed can grow differently from its parent even when it grows well.
